question: What is the primary underlying cause of inherited degenerative disorders?
explanation: These chronic conditions stem directly from inherited alterations in the patient's genetic code that drive tissue breakdown over time. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h1)

question: Why is early nursing intervention focused on anticipation rather than cure in degenerative disorders?

options.A: Genetic disorders progress rapidly within a few days
options.B: Patients usually recover spontaneously after middle age
options.C: Symptoms disappear completely with simple antibiotic therapy
options.D: The underlying genetic pathology is currently irreversible

explanation: Because these diseases steadily worsen without a cure, nursing care centers on planning for future functional loss. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h1)

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of advanced neurodegenerative conditions?

options.A: Progressive memory loss and cognitive decline
options.B: Rapid healing of damaged neural pathways
options.C: Sudden and complete recovery of motor function

explanation: Brain tissue deterioration consistently leads to a gradual decline in memory and executive functioning. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h2)

question: A patient with Huntington's disease develops jerky, involuntary limb movements. What term describes this neurological feature?
explanation: Chorea refers to the irregular, uncontrollable jerky movements frequently seen in certain inherited degenerative brain disorders. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h2)

question: What is the primary cause of joint contractures in long-term immobility?

options.A: High dietary intake of calcium and protein
options.B: Sudden bone growth in adult joints
options.C: Excessive daily physical exercise and stretching
options.D: Shortening and hardening of muscles and tendons

explanation: Lack of movement causes soft tissues around joints to shorten, producing fixed deformities known as contractures. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h3)

question: A bedridden patient with muscular dystrophy is at high risk for which musculoskeletal complication?

options.B: Increased bone density from constant pressure
options.D: Hypertrophy of lower extremity skeletal muscles

explanation: Immobility deprives bones of necessary weight-bearing stress, leading to mineral loss and weak bones prone to fractures. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h3)

question: Why are patients with degenerative neuromuscular diseases prone to recurrent pneumonia?

options.A: Overactive immune cells attack normal lung tissue
options.B: Rapid diaphragm movement forces bacteria into the lungs
options.C: Ineffective cough reflexes lead to sputum retention
options.D: Excessive surfactant production floods the alveoli

explanation: Weak respiratory muscles prevent forceful coughing, causing mucus to pool in the airways and harbor infectious agents. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h4)

question: What is a common cardiovascular consequence of autonomic nervous system dysfunction in degenerative disorders?
explanation: Autonomic failure impairs the body's ability to adjust blood vessel tone quickly when changing positions, causing blood pressure drops. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h4)

question: What term describes the difficulty in swallowing experienced by patients with advanced degenerative disorders?
explanation: Dysphagia refers specifically to swallowing impairments caused by muscle weakness or neurological damage. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h5)

question: Which intervention is most appropriate for managing chronic constipation caused by physical immobility?

options.A: Ensuring adequate fluid intake and dietary fiber
options.B: Eliminating physical movement entirely from the routine
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent fluid overload

explanation: Fiber and fluids add bulk and soften stool to compensate for slow bowel motility resulting from lack of exercise. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h5)

question: What is a common emotional challenge experienced by family members providing long-term care?
explanation: The endless demands of supporting a chronically ill family member frequently lead to severe emotional and physical fatigue. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h6)

question: Why is addressing the mental health of a patient with a degenerative disorder equally as important as physical care?

options.A: Depression and anxiety significantly diminish their quality of life
options.B: Mental distress stops the underlying genetic mutation from spreading
options.C: Emotional health cures respiratory complications completely
options.D: Psychological support replaces the need for any physical therapy

explanation: Psychological suffering impairs overall well-being and willingness to engage in necessary daily care routines. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h6)

question: A nurse cares for an immobile patient with muscle wasting. Which nursing action best prevents pressure injuries?

options.A: Massaging reddened skin areas with harsh alcohol rubs
options.B: Repositioning the patient on a regular, scheduled basis
options.C: Applying dry heat directly to all bony prominences
options.D: Keeping the patient in the exact same position all day

explanation: Regular turning relieves constant pressure on vulnerable tissues, maintaining adequate blood flow and preventing skin breakdown. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of performing passive range-of-motion exercises for a bedridden patient?

options.A: To reverse the inherited genetic mutation causing the disease
options.B: To eliminate the need for any nutritional support
options.C: To build massive new skeletal muscle mass independently
options.D: To prevent joint contractures and maintain tissue flexibility

explanation: Moving joints through their ranges manually stops soft tissues from tightening into permanent deformities. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h7)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for managing inherited degenerative disorders?

options.A: The conditions affect multiple body systems simultaneously
options.B: A single nurse cannot legally administer any oral medications
options.C: Specialists are required to cure the genetic defect
options.D: Hospital regulations forbid doctors from working alone

explanation: Complex multi-system deterioration requires diverse clinical expertise ranging from mobility to nutrition and breathing. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h8)

question: When is the most appropriate time to introduce palliative support in chronic degenerative diseases?

options.A: After all medical treatments have completely failed
options.B: When the patient requests a permanent cure
options.C: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.D: Early in the disease trajectory alongside active management

explanation: Early palliative care prioritizes comfort, symptom control, and quality of life from the time of diagnosis onward. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h8)
